note: B-/T-LBL relapsed ALL, RAS-pathway genes, ages 1-<21 all as stated. Genes published as Any Variation where text says activating/hotspot mutations or NF1 del (convention).
All melanomas, except ocular and mucosal melanoma; published Melanoma parent (7 codes) without excluding uveal/mucosal melanoma.

Phase 1 "Acute leukemia harboring KMT2A, NPM1 or nucleoporin alterations": KMT2A-r ALL not published (loses patients). KMT2A/NPM1 dropped as cohort_specific although every cohort requires one of them, so any AML matches; APL excluded in text but AML parent covers it (over-match).
Neuroblastoma, age >=12 months.
Stage M neuroblastoma, >=18 months and <18 years.
local or diffuse TGCT: OncoTree has only the diffuse type (TGCT), so the localized form has no code. Age >=12.

Part 1 lists "High and Low Grade Glioma: including GBM, DIPG, and ependymoma" and "Rhabdomyosarcoma"; published only High-Grade Glioma, NOS (1 code) and Embryonal Rhabdomyosarcoma, so LGG, GBM, DIPG/diffuse midline glioma, ependymoma and non-embryonal RMS patients are lost.

Locally confirmed dMMR or MSI-H disease: published requires mmr_status=MMR-Deficient AND ms_status=MSI-H, so a patient with only one of the two recorded is lost. BRAF V600E, colorectal adenocarcinoma, age >=16 correct.

r/r CD19-expressing ALL or NHL/CLL: Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma parent (87 codes) includes T- and NK-cell lymphomas, which are CD19-negative; the B-lineage restriction is only expressible through the diagnosis.
Solid tumour or NSCLC with ALK rearrangement or activating mutation; age >=12 is the union of cohort 2f (>=12) and the others (>=18).
CD19+ r/r B-ALL, 1 to 25 years (published <26).
r/r neuroblastoma, >1 and <18 years.

AML with KMT2A-r, NUP98-r or NPM1-mut, >30 days to <=18 years, all correct. Adds an exclusion the text does not state, NPM1 !Structural Variation (the text excludes KMT2A-PTD, not NPM1 rearrangements); affects only the rare NPM1-fusion AML.

allogenic transplant indication for ALL, no lineage: published only B-Lymphoblastic Leukemia/Lymphoma, so T-ALL patients are lost (the unqualified-ALL rule did not fire). Ages 3 months to <=25 correct.

Every phase requires an ALK, ROS1 or NTRK1-3 rearrangement, but the step-level criterion is _SOLID_ (651 codes) with no gene, so any advanced solid tumour matches; the only gene sits on one arm (ROS1 NSCLC), and the ALK and NTRK cohorts have none.

Transplant trial enrolling patients in remission ("Acute Leukemias: Must be in remission by morphology"; CR1 high-risk ALL and AML eligible), published with disease_status Refractory/Recurrent/Advanced on every diagnosis. Same finding as the 2026-09-29 Haiku audit of this trial.

Histopathological diagnosis of classical Hodgkin lymphoma, no stage restriction; published disease_status Untreated/Localized/Early Stage, which loses advanced-stage patients. Classical HL (NLPHL excluded) and ages 2-18 correct.

Cerebellar tumours "including ... anaplastic astrocytoma ... or other high-grade malignant tumor": anaplastic astrocytoma / high-grade glioma not published (only Glioblastoma, IDH-Wildtype among gliomas). Other listed types and ages 3-<22 correct.

NHL part names "DLBCL(NOS), follicular lymphoma, ... transforms DLBCL, PMBCL and high grade B cell lymphoma"; published Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma parent (88 codes) includes T/NK-cell lymphomas. B-ALL arm and ages correct.

Patients with histologically confirmed FLHCC: published also Hepatocellular Carcinoma, taken from registry condition terms ("Stage III Hepatocellular Carcinoma AJCC v8"), so all HCC patients match. disease_status Localized/Unresectable is questionable for a trial that counts extrahepatic disease as unresectable.

Cushing's disease, both new and previously diagnosed ("For newly diagnosed Cushing s disease cases, IPSS is required"); published disease_status Untreated/Localized loses previously treated patients. Diagnosis and age >=8 correct.

high-grade sarcomas of bone primary localisation, all soft tissue sarcomas excluded (E2); published Leiomyosarcoma, Angiosarcoma and UPS codes are soft-tissue codes. OncoTree has no bone-primary code for these, so the population cannot be stated exactly.
r/r CD19-positive leukaemia (conditions: relapsed/refractory ALL), <=21 years; B-ALL with Recurrent/Refractory.

ALK+ ALCL, IMT or Other Solid Tumors: ALK-positive other solid tumours (e.g. neuroblastoma) are not published, and the step-level Refractory/Recurrent status loses newly diagnosed unresectable IMT, which the text admits ("Newly diagnosed patients with unresectable ALK+ IMT ... may also be included").

Every cohort requires a ROS1 rearrangement, but the step-level criterion is _SOLID_ AND ROS1 !Any Variation (from the exclusion "known oncogenic driver alteration other than ROS1"): it matches every solid tumour without a ROS1 alteration and excludes exactly the eligible patients.

Recipients "Age 18-65 years"; published age >=12 (the related-donor age) and <121, so children 12-17 match although they are not eligible. disease_status Refractory/Recurrent/Advanced loses the eligible remission states ("AML with adverse cytogenetics ... regardless of remission status", "ALL in CR >= 2").
Frontline mature B-NHL protocol (Burkitt, DLBCL, PMBL, PCNSL, Burkitt leukaemia), 0-18 years, Untreated.
R/R aggressive mature B-NHL (BL, BAL, DLBCL, PMBCL), 6 months to <30 years.
R/R Ph- B-ALL: the Ph-negative requirement is not published (no BCR/ABL1 exclusion), so Ph+ B-ALL matches. Diagnosis, status and ages 15-70 correct.

Any malignancy with high TMB, MSI-high or CMMRD, in adult, paediatric and TYA patients. Published age <18 loses adults; the step-level tree has no biomarker, so every child with any cancer matches; the arm has mmr_status=!MMR-Deficient, which excludes exactly the CMMRD/dMMR patients the trial wants.
Refractory PML-RARA APL, 16-70. The fusion partner is published as "RARα" (fusion_partner_unverified) rather than RARA.

Text lists "glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), anaplastic astrocytoma (AA), fibrillary astrocytomas (FA), pilomyxoid astrocytoma (PXA), oligodendroglioma, or anaplastic mixed oligoastrocytoma (AOA), or ... (DIPG)"; published only DMG H3 K27-altered, GBM IDH-wildtype and pilomyxoid astrocytoma, so AA, diffuse/fibrillary astrocytoma, oligodendroglioma and oligoastrocytoma patients are lost.

Desmoid tumour progressing after watchful waiting, no prior antitumour agent, >=13: diagnosis and age correct, but disease_status Refractory/Advanced/Unresectable is not what the text says (untreated, progressive, ablatable), so patients recorded otherwise are lost.

all tumors considered low-grade glioma or low-grade astrocytoma (WHO grade I and II) with BRAF or CRAF alteration: published only Low-Grade Glioma, NOS and Diffuse LGG MAPK-altered (1 code each), so pilocytic astrocytoma, ganglioglioma and the other LGG codes - the commonest BRAF-altered paediatric LGGs - are lost. Genes and ages correct.
r/r B-ALL after CAR-T, 1-39 years.
Refractory retinoblastoma with RB1 mutation, >=6 months.
locally advanced or metastatic soft tissue or bone sarcoma plus a liposarcoma expansion cohort; published only Liposarcoma (5 codes), so every other soft tissue and bone sarcoma is lost.
r/r mature aggressive B-NHL in children (BL, DLBCL, PMBCL, Burkitt-like 11q, HGBCL), 6 months to <18.
Newly diagnosed AML with CEBPA bZIP mutation, 14 to <55 (AML parent plus a required CEBPA mutation).
r/r CD5+ T-ALL.
SDH-deficient GIST after >=1 systemic therapy, >=12 (SDHB loss is an IHC finding, not encodable).
r/r CD19+ B-ALL, >=14.
Newly diagnosed high-grade osteosarcoma, 14-70. The Osteosarcoma parent (11 codes) also covers low-grade subtypes, a minor over-match.

FLT3 expression must be detectable in AML blast by flow cytometric analysis (a CAR-T target): published as a required FLT3 Structural Variation, so FLT3-expressing AML without a FLT3 rearrangement - most patients - is lost. The same file lists FLT3 as gene_role_dropped (expression_or_germline) yet keeps it in the tree.
CD30+ lymphocyte malignancies: published only the one grey-zone code (B-cell lymphoma intermediate between DLBCL and cHL), so classical Hodgkin lymphoma, ALCL and other CD30+ lymphomas are lost.
PCNSL "without ... systemic lymphatic or hematopoietic involvement": published also Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma, NOS (3 codes), so systemic DLBCL matches.
All patients affected by Medulloblastoma operated on ... during their pediatric age: published disease_status Localized, so metastatic medulloblastoma is lost.

CD19 CAR-T for r/r B-ALL, a long list of B-cell lymphomas and myeloma. The step-level tree requires a MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement of every patient, taken from one listed subtype ("double or triple hit"), so B-ALL, myeloma and most lymphoma patients are lost. "ALK anaplastic large B-cell lymphoma" was published as Anaplastic Large-Cell Lymphoma ALK Positive, a T-cell lymphoma (over-match).

diffuse midline glioma (DMG) (H3 K27M mutant) or radiographic and/or pathologically proven pontine DMG: published Diffuse Glioma (24 codes, over-match) AND a required H3-3A variant, which loses H3C2 (HIST1H3B) K27M tumours and radiographically diagnosed pontine DMG without molecular results.

Has a metastatic or locally advanced and unresectable solid tumor (conditions also name HCC and biliary tract cancer; adolescents >=16 with Ewing sarcoma "or other malignancies"): published only Ewing Sarcoma, so every other advanced solid tumour is lost.
R/R osteosarcoma, >=12.
High-risk refractory or relapsed neuroblastoma/ganglioneuroblastoma, 18 months to 18 years.
RRMM with extramedullary/paramedullary disease; no age bound stated.

Intermediate-risk RMS is eligible "based upon FOXO1 fusion status": both fusion-negative (stage 2/3 group III; stage 4 <10 y) and fusion-positive. Published requires a FOXO1 Structural Variation of every patient, so fusion-negative RMS - most of the trial - is lost.
r/r CD19/CD20+ B-ALL, 12-75.
Newly diagnosed early-stage (I/II) non-bulky ... classical Hodgkin lymphoma: published also Hodgkin Lymphoma, which adds the HL parent and Nodular Lymphocyte-Predominant HL.
Has Philadelphia-negative disease: not published (no BCR/ABL1 exclusion), so Ph+ B-ALL matches. Diagnosis, status and age >=12 correct.

EGFR-positive tumours (protein expression; the trial needs a biomarker consent "for EGFR testing"): published as a required EGFR genomic variant (Any Variation), which most EGFR-expressing paediatric tumours do not carry. DIPG and "Other EGFR-positive solid tumor subtypes" from the list are also missing.

relapsed or refractory sarcoma (Phase 1) or osteosarcoma (Phase 2): published Osteosarcoma and Sarcoma, NOS (1 code), so every specific sarcoma (Ewing, rhabdomyosarcoma, synovial sarcoma, ...) is lost.
r/r high-risk MIBG-avid neuroblastoma, >=1 year.
